grammarPoint.title: Superlative adjectives
grammarPoint.summary: Use superlative adjectives to say something is the highest, lowest, or most extreme in a group of three or more.
grammarPoint.explanation:
We use superlative adjectives to compare three or more things and say which one has the most or least of a quality. For most short adjectives (one or two syllables), we add *-est* to the end of the adjective. Remember to use *the* before the superlative adjective.

For longer adjectives (three or more syllables), we use *the most* before the adjective. We do not change the adjective itself.

Some common adjectives have irregular superlative forms. The superlative of 'good' is *the best*, and the superlative of 'bad' is *the worst*. Always use *the* with these forms too.

examples.text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
examples.note: Shows that Mount Everest is at the top of a quality (height) compared to all other mountains.

examples.text: This is the smallest phone I've ever seen.
examples.note: Indicates this phone is at the bottom of a quality (size) compared to all other phones seen.

examples.text: That movie was the most interesting one this year.
examples.note: Highlights that the movie had the highest degree of 'interesting' compared to other movies this year.

examples.text: She makes the best cookies in the neighborhood.
examples.note: Uses the irregular superlative 'best' to show her cookies are superior to all others.

examples.text: The traffic today is the worst I've experienced.
examples.note: Uses the irregular superlative 'worst' to describe the lowest quality of traffic.

commonErrors.note: Always use 'the' before a superlative adjective.

commonErrors.wrong: This is the more beautiful song.
commonErrors.right: This is the most beautiful song.

commonErrors.wrong: He is the most tall student.

exercises.question: My dog is ___ in the park.
exercises.explanation: For short adjectives like 'fast', we add '-est' and use 'the' before it to form the superlative.

exercises.question: This book is ___ I've read all year.
exercises.explanation: For longer adjectives like 'interesting', we use 'the most' before the adjective.

exercises.question: That was ___ meal I've ever had!
Which is ___ animal on Earth?
exercises.explanation: For short adjectives like 'big', we add '-est' and double the consonant before adding '-est'.

exercises.text: This is ___ (tall) building in the city.
exercises.explanation: For the short adjective 'tall', we add '-est' and 'the' to form the superlative.
For the long adjective 'difficult', we use 'the most' before it to form the superlative.

exercises.text: Yesterday was ___ (bad) day of the week.
exercises.explanation: The irregular superlative form of 'bad' is 'worst'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: The sentence uses 'the fastest' to describe the car as having the highest speed compared to others.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: The sentence uses 'the most careful' to describe the driver as having the highest degree of carefulness.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: That was the more delicious cake.
answers: That was the most delicious cake.
exercises.explanation: For longer adjectives like 'delicious', we use 'the most' to form the superlative, not 'the more'.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: She is the goodest student in the class.
answers: She is the best student in the class.
exercises.explanation: The superlative form of 'good' is 'best', not 'goodest'.

exercises.source: No other city is as big as Tokyo.
exercises.explanation: The superlative form 'the biggest' shows that Tokyo is unmatched in size compared to other cities.

exercises.source: This is a very bad movie.
exercises.explanation: The word 'worst' is the superlative form of 'bad', indicating the lowest quality.
